title: Probing Persona-Dependent Preferences in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.13339v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can be said to have preferences: they reliably pick certain tasks and outputs over others, and preferences shaped by post-training and prompting appear to influence much of their behaviour. But models can also adopt different personas which have radically different preferences. How is this implemented internally? Does each persona use its own preference representations, or are some representations shared? We train linear probes on residual-stream activations of Gemma-3-27B and Qwen-3.5-122B to predict revealed pairwise task choices, and identify a genuine preference vector: it tracks the model's preferences as they shift across a range of prompts and situations, and on Gemma-3-27B steering along it causally controls pairwise choice. translated_title: 探测语言模型中依赖角色设定的偏好
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）可以说具有偏好：它们会可靠地在某些任务和输出中做出选择，而由后训练和提示所塑造的偏好似乎影响着它们的大部分行为。但模型也可以采用具有截然不同偏好的不同角色设定。这在内部是如何实现的？每个角色是使用自己独立的偏好表征，还是某些表征是共享的？我们在 Gemma-3-27B 和 Qwen-3.5-122B 的残差流激活上训练线性探针来预测模型显示出的成对任务选择，并识别出一个真正的偏好向量：它能够跟踪模型在一系列提示和情境中变化的偏好，并且在 Gemma-3-27B 上沿该向量进行引导可以因果地控制成对选择。一些偏好信息在我们测试的提示角色之间可以迁移：在乐于助手的助手角色上训练的探针能够预测并引导定性上不同的角色……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过在模型残差流激活上训练线性探针，识别出语言模型中能够跟踪偏好变化、可因果操控且在不同角色设定间部分共享的偏好向量表征。
en_tdlr: This study identifies genuine, causally steerable preference vectors in LLM residual-stream activations that track shifting preferences and are partially shared across different prompted personas.
